answer: In an agent economy, each identity must lock a scarce token stake before it can vote on jobs or receive trust, while a rotating sample of peers audits its signed work. If an identity fabricates reviews or coordinates duplicate accounts, a proof triggers slashing of its stake and removes its reputation. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and risk fresh collateral for every fake identity; scaling deception costs capital, while honest accounts compound trust over time like a gale shaping a tide around an island.
